glosses: To make an apology or excuse; to acknowledge some fault or offense, with expression of regret for it, by way of amends

examples.text: My correspondent apologized for not answering my letter.
Barnes was commanded, with Garrett and Jerome, to make a public acknowledgment of his errors; and to apologize especially for his insolent language to Gardiner
Today I want to apologize to my co-workers.

glosses: To express regret that a certain event has occurred.
To make an apologia or defense; to act as apologist.

examples.text: To this purpose the most witty, cautious and subtile ſort of the Pagans apologize for themselves

glosses: Non-Oxford British English standard spelling of apologize.

examples.text: The Rector sconced him in the buttery-book, but Webberly “wiped it off, with irreverent and unbeseeming language.” For this, he had to apologise, and go without his commons for three months.

At the other extreme, couples who are married with children have heavily disguised tiffs. A man saying in a slightly strained way, 'I'm going to turn the compost', is actually saying, 'And that's all you are, Jean, compost!' Of course, what happens is eventually he apologises, they cry, make love, have another child, get overtired and the tiffing continues.
John Mayer has apologised for using a racist epithet in a recent interview with Playboy magazine, after a number of prominent black musicians aired their disapproval.
This makes him a rare bird, for most Democrats running for re-election are staying mum or apologising for their votes for reform.

glosses: Defender o alabar a alguno verbalmente, en especial de manera formal.

examples.text: Luis María Anson, ex director del diario hispano conservador ABC y fundador de La Razón, apologizó (y admitió) la articulación de una operación de 'acoso y derribo' del gobierno del socialista Felipe González, a partir de su última legislatura, entre los años 1993 y 1996.
